mainTopic: Cures for a כלב שוטה's rub and bite, and רבי יוחנן's treatment of צפדינא on שבת in light of רבי מתיא בן חרש
overview: This amud finishes שמואל's rule that a כלב שוטה (mad dog) must be killed only with a thrown object, and a ברייתא supports him. The ברייתא adds that being rubbed by the dog is dangerous and being bitten is deadly, and the גמרא gives a cure for each. For a rub, strip off your clothes and run, as רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע did. For a bite, אביי prescribes an amulet on hyena skin, burying and burning the clothes, and drinking only through a metal tube for twelve months. The גמרא then turns to רבי מתיא בן חרש's ruling in the משנה about putting medicine in a painful mouth on שבת. It tells how רבי יוחנן got a cure for צפדינא from a matron, swore secrecy with careful wording, and taught it publicly. The גמרא explains how this was neither a broken oath nor a חילול השם. It then lists the remedy, the cause and the sign of the disease. It explains that רבי יוחנן could treat it on שבת because צפדינא reaches the intestines and is dangerous. רבי יוחנן tells רב חייא בר אבא that the חכמים agree with רבי מתיא only in this case. The גמרא tries to prove this from the word 'these' (בְּאֵילּוּ) in two ברייתות, and every proof in both directions is turned aside.

steps.title: Kill a mad dog only from a distance
steps.stepSummary: The end of שמואל's statement: a mad dog should be killed with a thrown object.
steps.simpleTranslation: …to kill it with something that is thrown.
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing שמואל's rule from the previous section: when you kill a כלב שוטה, do it with something thrown, not with your hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dog is thought to be possessed by an evil spirit, so direct contact is dangerous. Using a thrown object, like an arrow or stone, keeps you from touching it.

phrases.english: to kill it with a thrown object.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes שמואל's statement begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mad dog must be killed only with a thrown object, never by hand.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports שמואל and lists the dog's dangers
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא matches שמואל's rule and adds that a rub is dangerous and a bite is deadly.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in line with שמואל: when you kill a mad dog, kill it only with a thrown object. Someone the dog rubs against is in danger. Someone it bites will die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as שמואל. The ברייתא also adds two new facts about the dog.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase תניא כוותיה means that an earlier, authoritative source agrees with the אמורא. The ברייתא also brings in two new cases, a rub and a bite. The next steps will discuss each of them.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא in agreement with him

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Shmuel:
When they kill it,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הוֹרְגִין אוֹתוֹ אֶלָּא בְּדָבָר הַנִּזְרָק.
phrases.english: they kill it only with a thrown object.
One that it rubs against is endangered;
one that it bites dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's rule with a תנאי source.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that a mad dog is killed only with a thrown object.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating the same rule.

steps.title: What is the cure for someone the dog rubbed against?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the remedy for someone rubbed by a mad dog.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One that it rubs against is endangered.' What is his fix?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first danger from the ברייתא and asks what such a person should do. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only said a rub is dangerous. Now the גמרא wants a practical solution.

phrases.english: 'One that it rubs against is endangered':
What is his remedy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the first danger listed in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A remedy for someone rubbed by a mad dog.

steps.title: Take off your clothes and run
steps.stepSummary: The cure for a rub is to remove one's clothing and run away.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should throw off his clothes and run.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the person should strip off his clothes and run away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger seems to stay with the clothes that touched the dog. Taking them off and running separates the person from that danger.

keyTerms.meaning: let him take off his clothes

phrases.english: Let him remove his clothes and run.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about a rub.

steps.title: רב הונא used this cure in the market
steps.stepSummary: A story: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע was rubbed by a mad dog, stripped, and ran.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע was rubbed by one of these dogs in the market. He threw off his clothes and ran. He said: I fulfilled in myself the verse 'Wisdom keeps alive those who have it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case where a חכם used this exact cure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows the cure was used in practice. רב הונא credits his Torah knowledge with saving his life, and he quotes a פסוק from קהלת.

keyTerms.meaning: wisdom keeps its owners alive (קהלת ז:יב)

phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua:
one of them (mad dogs) rubbed against him in the market;
he threw off his clothes and ran.
He said: I fulfilled in myself
'Wisdom gives life to those who have it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ חַף בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the remedy just given.
steps.raayaObject: The cure of stripping and running.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The real-life incident of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.

steps.title: What is the cure for someone the dog bit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the second, deadlier case: a bite.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One that it bites dies.' What is his fix?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the second danger from the ברייתא, a bite, and asks for its cure. It is setting up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bite is far more serious than a rub, since the ברייתא said the person 'dies.' So we should expect a much more elaborate remedy.

phrases.english: 'One that it bites dies':
What is his remedy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rub case to the bite case listed in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A remedy for someone bitten by a mad dog.

steps.title: אביי's amulet on hyena skin
steps.stepSummary: אביי says to write a special formula, with divine names, on the skin of a male hyena.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Bring the skin of a male hyena and write on it: 'I, so-and-so son of so-and-so, write about you on the skin of a male hyena: kanti kanti kelirus.' Some say: 'kandi kandi keloros, Yah Yah, ה׳ of Hosts, amen amen selah.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins his cure for a bite. The first part is writing a protective formula on hyena skin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The formula names the person and his mother, then uses unusual words and ה׳'s names. ואמרי לה brings a second version of the wording.
steps.confusionAlert: The strange words (כנתי, קלירוס, and the like) are not Aramaic words you are supposed to translate. They are the text of an incantation formula.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Let him bring the skin of a male hyena
and write on it:
'I, so-and-so son of so-and-so (fem.),
on the skin of a male hyena I write about you:
"Kanti kanti kelirus."'
And some say: "Kandi kandi keloros,

phrases.aramaic: יָהּ יָהּ ה׳ צְבָאוֹת אָמֵן אָמֵן סֶלָה״.
phrases.english: Yah Yah, Lord of Hosts, amen amen selah."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי נֵיתֵי מַשְׁכָּא דְּאַפָּא דִּיכְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question about a bite.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Write a specific protective formula on male hyena skin.

steps.title: Bury the clothes, then burn them and scatter the ashes
steps.stepSummary: Next, אביי says to bury the clothes in a cemetery for twelve months, then burn them and scatter the ashes at a crossroads.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should take off his clothes and bury them in a cemetery for twelve months. Then he takes them out, burns them in an oven, and scatters the ashes at a crossroads.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues the cure. The clothes the person wore must be removed and destroyed in stages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As with the rub case, the clothing is treated as carrying the danger. Here, though, it is not simply thrown off. It is buried for a year, burned, and scattered.

phrases.english: And let him take off his clothes
and bury them in a cemetery
for twelve months of the year,
then take them out and burn them in an oven
and scatter their ashes at a crossroads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's remedy.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bury the clothes for twelve months, then burn them and scatter the ashes at a crossroads.

steps.title: Drink only through a copper tube for the year
steps.stepSummary: During those twelve months, he must drink only through a copper tube so he does not see a demon's reflection.
steps.simpleTranslation: During those twelve months, when he drinks water, he should drink only through a copper tube. Otherwise he might see the reflection of the demon and be endangered.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a final precaution for the twelve months: don't look at water while drinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that he will see the image of the שד (demon) in the water. A tube lets him drink without looking at the water's surface.

phrases.english: And during those twelve months of the year,
when he drinks water,
let him drink only through a copper tube,
lest he see the demon's reflection and be endangered.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנָךְ תְּרֵיסַר יַרְחֵי שַׁתָּא כִּי שָׁתֵי מַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a precaution to the same remedy.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For twelve months, drink only through a copper tube.

steps.title: אבא בר מרתא's mother made him a gold tube
steps.stepSummary: An example: אבא בר מרתא (also called אבא בר מניומי) drank through a gold tube his mother made.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the case of אבא בר מרתא, who is אבא בר מניומי: his mother made him a gold tube.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a real example of someone who used a drinking tube. His wealthy mother even made his tube out of gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the practice was actually followed. It also shows that a tube of another metal, here gold, was used for the same purpose.
steps.whatToRemember: Rub: strip and run. Bite: אביי's full process of amulet, burying and burning the clothes, and a drinking tube for twelve months.

phrases.english: Like that of Abba bar Marta,
who is Abba bar Manyumi:
his mother made him a gold tube.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the tube precaution.
steps.raayaObject: Drinking through a metal tube during the year.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of אבא בר מרתא's gold tube.

steps.title: Back to רבי מתיא: רבי יוחנן seeks a cure for צפדינא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבי מתיא's ruling in the משנה and tells how רבי יוחנן went to a gentile matron to treat צפדינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And further said רבי מתיא…' רבי יוחנן suffered from צפדינא. He went to a certain matron, and she prepared a treatment for him on Thursday and Friday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה, where רבי מתיא allows putting medicine in the mouth of someone with throat pain on שבת. It opens a related story about רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: צפדינא is a disease that starts in the mouth and gums, which fits רבי מתיא's case of mouth and throat pain. The matron treated him on weekdays, and this sets up his question about שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and further said רבי מתיא' (quoting the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי מתיא (the תנא in the משנה) with רבי יוחנן. רבי מתיא's name is only the heading; the story is about רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: 'And further, Rabbi Matya said':
Rabbi Yochanan suffered from tzefidna.
He went to a certain matron;

phrases.aramaic: עֲבַדָא לֵיהּ מִלְּתָא חַמְשָׁא וּמַעֲלֵי שַׁבְּתָא.
phrases.english: she made him a remedy on Thursday and Friday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the mad dog topic and returns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opens the discussion of רבי מתיא's allowance to treat mouth and throat pain on שבת, through רבי יוחנן's story.

steps.title: What about שבת?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks what he will do on שבת. She says he won't need it, and he asks what if he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: What about on שבת? She said: You won't need it. He asked: And if I do need it, what then?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן worries he won't be able to get treatment on שבת, so he presses the matron for a backup plan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He cannot come to her on שבת, so he wants to know the remedy himself. His follow-up question shows he wants to be ready in case of danger.

phrases.english: He said to her: What about on Shabbat?
She said to him: You will not need it.
If I do need it, what then?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with רבי יוחנן's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי יוחנן could get the cure on שבת if needed.

steps.title: She demands an oath of secrecy
steps.stepSummary: The matron agrees to tell him only if he swears not to reveal it, and he swears 'to the God of Israel.'
steps.simpleTranslation: She said: Swear to me that you won't reveal it. He swore: 'To the God of Israel, I will not reveal it.'
steps.whatsHappening: She agrees to share the secret remedy only if he takes an oath of secrecy, and he swears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pay attention to the exact wording of his oath: 'לאלהא דישראל לא מגלינא.' The coming גמרא will analyze this phrasing.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: אִישְׁתְּבַע לִי דְּלָא מְגַלֵּית,
phrases.english: She said to him: Swear to me that you will not reveal it.
He swore: 'To the God of Israel, I will not reveal.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Her condition for answering his question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She will reveal the remedy only in exchange for an oath of secrecy.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן taught it publicly
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן went out and taught the remedy in his public lecture.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went out and expounded it in the public lecture.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רבי יוחנן revealing the secret cure publicly. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will ask how he could break his oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This looks like a violation of his oath, which is the obvious problem the next passage takes up. By teaching it publicly, he made a lifesaving cure available to everyone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a famous question: how could a צדיק like רבי יוחנן appear to break an oath? The answer will depend on the exact wording he used.

phrases.english: He went out and taught it in the public lecture.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the apparent breach of the oath he just took.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן revealed the remedy publicly, which sets up the challenge about his oath.

steps.title: But he swore not to reveal it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's public teaching of the remedy, since he swore to the matron that he would keep it secret.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he swore to her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised. How could רבי יוחנן teach the remedy in public after swearing he would not reveal it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said he taught the remedy openly, and step 13 said he took an oath. These two facts seem to clash, and the גמרא points this out.

phrases.english: But he swore to her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the action described in step 14 using the oath from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's public teaching of the remedy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Revealing the secret seems to break his explicit oath.

steps.title: The oath covered only the God of Israel
steps.stepSummary: The wording of the oath was 'to the God of Israel I will not reveal it.' That wording leaves room to reveal it to His people, Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: [He swore:] 'To the God of Israel I will not reveal it.' This implies: to His people Israel, I will reveal it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן worded his oath cleverly. He swore not to reveal it 'to the God of Israel,' not 'by' Him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The matron heard 'I swear by the God of Israel,' but the words can also mean 'I will not reveal it TO the God of Israel.' Read that way, telling the Jewish people is not covered by the oath.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase in step 13 sounded like an oath BY God. The גמרא now reads it as 'I won't tell it TO God,' which leaves the people of Israel outside the oath.

phrases.english: To the God of Israel I will not reveal it.
Implying: to His people Israel, I will reveal it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the exact wording of the oath
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The oath forbade revealing the remedy to anyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The oath only excluded revealing it 'to the God of Israel,' so revealing it to the Jewish people is allowed.

steps.title: But this desecrates God's name
steps.stepSummary: Even if no oath was technically broken, the matron will think a great rabbi broke his oath. That is a חילול השם.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is still a desecration of God's name!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further. Even with the clever wording, it looks bad, because the matron will think רבי יוחנן broke his word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer solves the technical problem of the oath. It does not solve how things appear to an outsider, which is what this challenge is about.

phrases.english: But there is a desecration of God's name!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the answer of step 16 is enough.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer about the oath's wording
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Technically keeping the oath still looks like breaking it, which causes a חילול השם.

steps.title: He told her from the start
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן told the matron right away that his oath would not stop him from publicizing the remedy.
steps.simpleTranslation: He revealed it to her at the outset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there was no חילול השם. רבי יוחנן told the matron right away how his oath was meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once she knew his true intent from the start, she could not feel deceived. So nobody would think he broke his word.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, at the outset

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's oath was worded 'to the God of Israel,' and he told the matron his intent at once. So there was neither a broken oath nor a חילול השם.

phrases.english: He revealed it to her at the outset.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17 and closes the oath discussion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The matron was misled, so God's name was desecrated.
steps.terutzMaskana: She was told immediately, so no one was deceived.

steps.title: What remedy did she make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the matron actually prepared for רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did she prepare for him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the oath to the medicine itself. This question sets up the next step, which lists the opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a factual question about the content of the remedy. It is not a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: What did she make for him?

phrases.english: What did she prepare for him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the oath to the content of the remedy.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The ingredients of the remedy for צפדינא

steps.title: Three opinions about the remedy
steps.stepSummary: Three אמוראים give three versions of the remedy. רב אחא says leaven water, olive oil, and salt. רב יימר says leaven itself, olive oil, and salt. רב אשי says fat from a goose's wing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב אמי said: leaven water, olive oil, and salt. רב יימר said: the leaven itself, olive oil, and salt. רב אשי said: fat from a goose's wing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings three different answers to what the remedy was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא and רב יימר differ only on whether the leaven was soaked in water or used as is. רב אשי names a completely different remedy.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rav Ami said:
Leaven water, olive oil, and salt.
Rav Yeimar said:
The leaven itself, olive oil, and salt.
Rav Ashi said:
Fat from a goose's wing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.

steps.title: אביי's remedy from an Arab
steps.stepSummary: אביי says none of those remedies cured him. An Arab taught him to burn unripe olive pits on a new hoe and apply them to the gums, and that worked.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: I tried all of them and was not cured. Then a certain Arab told me: bring olive pits that have not reached a third of ripeness, burn them in a fire on a new hoe, and stick them along the gums. I did this and was cured.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds his own experience. He offers a remedy that actually worked for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not argue about what the matron used. He tells the reader which cure proved effective in practice.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
I did all of them and was not cured,
until a certain Arab told me:
Bring olive pits
that have not reached a third (of ripeness),
and burn them in fire on a new hoe,
and stick it along the rows of the gums.
I did this and was cured.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a tested remedy after the three opinions in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burned unripe olive pits applied to the gums cure צפדינא.

steps.title: What causes the illness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where צפדינא comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: From what does it come?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about the cause of the disease. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having discussed the cure, the גמרא turns to the cause. This is an informational question, not a challenge.

phrases.english: From what does it come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the remedy to the cause of the disease.

steps.title: Caused by hot wheat bread and fried fish leftovers
steps.stepSummary: צפדינא comes from eating very hot wheat bread and leftover fish fried in oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: From very hot wheat [bread] and from the leftovers of a cup of fish fried in oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers what causes the illness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two foods are named as causes: wheat bread eaten too hot, and leftover fried fish.

phrases.english: From very hot wheat [bread],
and from the leftovers of a cup of fried fish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Very hot wheat bread and leftover fried fish

steps.title: The sign of the illness
steps.stepSummary: The sign of צפדינא is that when a person puts something between his teeth, blood comes from the gums.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is its sign? When one puts something between his teeth, blood comes from the gums.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how to recognize the illness. It asks the question and answers it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bleeding gums when biting identify the disease. This matters because the next steps treat צפדינא as a special, dangerous case.

phrases.english: And what is its sign?
When one puts something between his teeth,
and blood comes out from the gums.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the symptom after the cause in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bleeding gums when biting is the sign of צפדינא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן treated himself on שבת
steps.stepSummary: When רבי יוחנן suffered from צפדינא, he applied this remedy on שבת and was cured.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יוחנן suffered from צפדינא, he did this on שבת and was healed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that רבי יוחנן used the remedy on שבת. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This brings the discussion back to the הלכות of שבת. Treating a mouth ailment on שבת normally seems to be a problem.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan, when he suffered from tzefidna,
did this on Shabbat and was cured.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from medical details to the שבת issue.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן applied the remedy on שבת.

steps.title: How could רבי יוחנן do this on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן could treat what looks like a minor mouth ailment on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how did רבי יוחנן do this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's action. Gum disease does not seem dangerous enough to justify treatment on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Healing on שבת is normally permitted only when there is danger. A mouth sore seems like a non-dangerous illness, so the action looks forbidden.

phrases.english: And how did Rabbi Yochanan do this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the action reported in step 25.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A gum ailment seems non-dangerous, so treating it on שבת should be forbidden.

steps.title: צפדינא starts in the mouth but reaches the intestines
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that צפדינא is different. It begins in the mouth but ends in the intestines, so it is dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: צפדינא is different, since it begins in the mouth and ends in the intestines.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that this illness is actually dangerous, so treating it on שבת is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The illness looks minor because it shows up in the mouth. In reality it spreads inward to the intestines, so it counts as פיקוח נפש.
steps.whatToRemember: צפדינא may be treated on שבת because, although it starts in the mouth, it reaches the intestines and is dangerous.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Tzefidna is different,
since it begins in the mouth,
and ends in the intestines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: צפדינא is a minor mouth ailment.
steps.terutzMaskana: It spreads to the intestines, so it is a danger to life.

steps.title: Was רבי יוחנן following רבי מתיא בן חרש?
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבא asks רבי יוחנן whether he acted like רבי מתיא בן חרש, who permits putting medicine in a painful mouth on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אבא said to רבי יוחנן: Whose view are you following? Is it רבי מתיא בן חרש, who said that one whose mouth hurts may have medicine put in it on שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בר אבא asks רבי יוחנן which opinion he relied on. He suggests it was רבי מתיא בן חרש from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מתיא בן חרש's view in the משנה seems to be a minority opinion. The question implies it would be odd for רבי יוחנן to rely on it.

keyTerms.meaning: One who has pain in his mouth

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Chiya bar Abba said to Rabbi Yochanan:
According to whom? According to Rabbi Matya ben Charash,
who said: one who has pain in his mouth,
they put medicine in it for him on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כְּמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects רבי יוחנן's action back to רבי מתיא's ruling in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוחנן relied on רבי מתיא בן חרש's seemingly minority view

steps.title: Only in this case, and no other
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the חכמים agree with רבי מתיא in this case of צפדינא, but not in other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: For I say [that the חכמים agree] in this case, and not in any other.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains that he is not relying on a lone opinion. Everyone agrees about this specific illness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because צפדינא is dangerous, even the חכמים who argue with רבי מתיא allow treating it on שבת. The agreement is limited to this case.
steps.whatToRemember: The ruling of רבי מתיא בן חרש about mouth pain is accepted by everyone for צפדינא, since it is dangerous, but it does not extend to other cases.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying he follows רבי מתיא in general. He is saying that in this one dangerous case the חכמים agree too.

phrases.english: He said to him:
For I say: in this case, and not in another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חייא בר אבא's question in step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים agree with רבי מתיא in the case of צפדינא only.

steps.title: A ברייתא that may support רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא listing רבי מתיא בן חרש's remedies, where the חכמים say 'these' have no healing value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this supports him: Someone seized with ירקון is fed donkey meat. Someone bitten by a mad dog is fed the lobe of its liver. Someone with mouth pain may have medicine put in his mouth on שבת. These are the words of רבי מתיא בן חרש. The חכמים say: 'these' have no healing value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא as a possible proof for רבי יוחנן. This step sets up the source, and the next step will draw the inference from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the חכמים agree with רבי מתיא about mouth medicine. The ברייתא lists three remedies of רבי מתיא, and the חכמים reject 'these'. The word 'these' (בְּאֵילּוּ) will become the key to the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say [this source] supports him

phrases.english: Let us say that this supports him:
One who is seized with yerakon —
we feed him donkey meat;
one whom a mad dog bit —
we feed him the lobe of its liver;
and one who has pain in his mouth —
we put medicine in it on Shabbat;
these are the words of Rabbi Matya ben Charash.
And the Sages say:
These have no value as a remedy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support רבי יוחנן's answer in step 29.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that the חכמים agree about mouth medicine (צפדינא).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing רבי מתיא בן חרש's three remedies.

steps.title: The word 'these' seems to leave out the mouth medicine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'these' excludes and suggests it excludes the mouth medicine, which would mean the חכמים agree about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'These' comes to exclude what? Is it not to exclude the medicine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof from the word 'these'. It suggests the חכמים meant only the first two remedies, not the mouth medicine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים had rejected everything, they would not need to say 'these'. Saying 'these' suggests some item was left out of the rejection, most likely the mouth medicine. That would match רבי יוחנן exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not...? (introduces a suggested reading)

phrases.english: 'These': to exclude what?
Is it not to exclude the medicine?

steps.triggerLanguage: ״בְּאֵלּוּ״ לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי? מַאי לָאו, לְמַעוֹטֵי סַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the actual inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 30.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים agree with רבי מתיא about mouth medicine.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The limiting word בְּאֵילּוּ in the ברייתא.

steps.title: No: 'these' excludes bloodletting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. 'These' may exclude a different ruling of רבי מתיא: bloodletting for סרונכי.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It excludes: 'we let blood for סרונכי.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The word 'these' could be leaving out a different remedy that רבי מתיא taught elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מתיא had another ruling that does not appear in this ברייתא: bloodletting for סרונכי. 'These' could be excluding that ruling, which the חכמים do accept as a real cure. So the ברייתא no longer proves anything about the mouth medicine.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain illness (often explained as a throat or chest ailment)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the mouth medicine is forbidden. The גמרא is only saying this ברייתא cannot prove that it is permitted.

phrases.english: No, it comes to exclude:
'We let blood for serunkhi.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 31.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from this ברייתא. רבי יוחנן's ruling itself is not attacked.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'These' could exclude a ruling outside the list (bloodletting), not the mouth medicine.

steps.title: A second ברייתא shows bloodletting was one of רבי מתיא's rulings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the rejection with a ברייתא in which רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי lists three rulings of רבי מתיא, starting with bloodletting for סרונכי.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also logical, as it was taught: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי said three things he heard in the name of רבי מתיא בן חרש. We let blood for סרונכי on שבת. Someone bitten by a mad dog is fed the lobe of its liver. Someone with mouth pain may have medicine put in his mouth on שבת. The חכמים say: 'these' have no healing value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the rejection. Another ברייתא shows that bloodletting really was one of רבי מתיא's rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rejection in step 32 relied on רבי מתיא having a bloodletting ruling. This ברייתא confirms he had one, and it ends with the same 'these' from the חכמים. The proof itself comes in the next step, which reads that word as excluding bloodletting.

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable.
As it was taught: three things
Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei said

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁשָּׁמַע מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מַתְיָא בֶּן חָרָשׁ:
phrases.english: that he heard in the name of Rabbi Matya ben Charash:
We let blood for serunkhi on Shabbat;
and one whom a mad dog bit —
we feed him the lobe of its liver;

phrases.aramaic: וְהַחוֹשֵׁשׁ בְּפִיו מְטִילִין לוֹ סַם בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: and one with pain in his mouth, we put medicine in it on Shabbat.
And the Sages say:
These have no value as a remedy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in step 32.
steps.raayaObject: That bloodletting for סרונכי was a ruling of רבי מתיא, so 'these' could exclude it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי.

steps.title: In the second ברייתא, 'these' seems to exclude only the first item
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that in the second ברייתא, 'these' refers to the last two items and excludes the first. That would mean the חכמים reject the mouth medicine.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'These' comes to exclude what? Is it not referring to the last two, and excluding the first?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem from the second ברייתא. If 'these' means the last two items, the mouth medicine is among the remedies the חכמים reject.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the חכמים would accept bloodletting, the first item, and reject the dog-liver remedy and the mouth medicine. That contradicts רבי יוחנן, who said the חכמים agree about mouth medicine.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the first part (the opening item)

phrases.english: 'These': to exclude what?
Is it not referring to the last two
and excluding the first one!

steps.triggerLanguage: ״בְּאֵילּוּ״ לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי? מַאי לָאו, אַתַּרְתֵּי בָּתְרָיָיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the 'these' of the ברייתא just brought in step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim (step 29) that the חכמים agree about mouth medicine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'these' excludes only bloodletting, then the mouth medicine falls inside the חכמים's rejection.

steps.title: No: 'these' refers to the first two and excludes the last
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'these' refers to the first two items of the first ברייתא (ירקון and the dog's liver) and excludes the last item, the mouth medicine.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It refers to the first two at the beginning, and excludes the last item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem. 'These' can be read as the first two items listed in the first ברייתא (ירקון and the dog's liver), which leaves the mouth medicine outside the חכמים's rejection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the item the חכמים agree to is the last one, the mouth medicine. So רבי יוחנן's claim stands. The ברייתא can be read either way, so it does not prove the opposite.

keyTerms.meaning: Referring to the first two at the beginning
Of the last part (the final item)

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'these' (בְּאֵילּוּ) can be read in more than one way. The גמרא ends with a reading in which the חכמים agree that mouth medicine for צפדינא is allowed on שבת, matching רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: No: it refers to the first two of the first [baraita],
and excludes the last one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading which items the word 'these' refers to.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'These' meant the last two items, so the חכמים reject the mouth medicine.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'These' means the first two items of the first ברייתא (ירקון and the dog's liver), so the mouth medicine is excluded from the rejection and the חכמים agree to it.
